acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Serpents family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Adder, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Range-Probe Initiate archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Small thick-bodied viper with zigzag markings, short fangs, keeled scales, and a compact tail.
Signature mechanic: One-Length Strike: the Adder's extension never exceeds the length stored in its single tight coil.
battlefieldDuty: Coil once and strike exactly one body length.
constructionDimensions: Scales, belly scutes, fangs, venom, shed skin, dust, saliva, and muscle remain ordinary and species-specific.
Coils and attack lines read through body tension, scale overlap, head position, and terrain contact.
counterplay: Step beyond the fixed reach and punish the fully extended neck. Affinity signal: The neck S, anchored head, hood alignment, surface horn, or lifting crown scale remains visible before commitment.
forbiddenTreatments: Humanoid torso, arms, clothing, or weapons
identityInvariants: Every form remains limbless with a continuous scaled body, snake skull, jaw hinge, belly scutes, forked tongue, and species-appropriate tail.
Tier escalation uses body proportion, hood, fangs, horns, crown scales, muscle distribution, and coil behavior rather than arms or equipment.
Strike range, head anchor, venom direction, emergence point, and loosened coil remain visually traceable.
telegraph: Its neck forms a tight S and the forked tongue stops flicking.
